{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693605266,"sessionID":"ses_e23eecba8ffen2PZwRCFwmWHj7","part":{"id":"prt_1dc1325ec001oDOcw3iHsb00k5","messageID":"msg_1dc1303070012WNJvLr5ArIEcB","sessionID":"ses_e23eecba8ffen2PZwRCFwmWHj7","type":"text","text":"The shift is over, and all four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from minute 66 to the end (minute 120). The worst cost of the shift was one I caused: rolling back seo-svc set off a retry storm that knocked out about 70% of admin-portal, the highest-revenue service, for several minutes.\n\n**What I found and did**\n\n1. **web-storefront and mobile-api (~90% errors since minute −25).** A profile-svc deploy (v94) raised the minimum TLS version to 1.3, and its logs showed \"TLS handshake failed: protocol version\" errors. I rolled it back.\n   - profile-svc depends on couriers-svc, and couriers-svc had been overloaded since minute −10. Its incoming traffic had grown from about 333 to about 860 requests/min, beyond what 4 replicas can serve, and retries made up 72% of its load.\n   - I throttled couriers-svc to 85% to stop the retries, scaled it to 12 replicas, then lifted the throttle. It is now at 10 replicas, which costs $18/min until the end of the shift.\n2. **admin-portal (steady ~4% errors).** The errors came through experiments-svc, which was getting \"429 rate limiter bucket empty\" from seo-svc. An seo-svc deploy (v30) had broken the rate limiter's refill calculation, so I rolled it back.\n   - **My mistake:** seo-svc was already at about 87% CPU. The failures during the rollback were retried, which overloaded it and pushed admin-portal to roughly 70% errors at about $20,400/min. I throttled seo-svc to 60% for two minutes and errors went to 0 at minute 45. I should have throttled first or added capacity before rolling back.\n3. **New fault at minute 55: web-storefront and partner-api at ~66% errors.** A thumbnails-svc config change (cfg-39) switched `wire_schema` from v2 to v3, causing DecodeErrors. I reverted the config and errors were back to 0 at minute 66.\n\nI left currency-svc alone even though its CPU alert has been firing since minute −10: none of the four customer-facing services depends on it, so a mitigation would probably have been a $10,000 wasted-action charge. I also changed nothing on experiments-svc, since its errors came from seo-svc.","time":{"start":1794693604844,"end":1794693605263}}}
